title: Elastic column collapse, proportional-resize heuristics and density-tuning surface
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers using very wide datasets frequently need to condense column real estate without losing discoverability or breaking keyboard/screen-reader flows. Current table variants enumerate density presets but lack an integrated surface for tuning density, and proportional-resize heuristics cause jarring layout jumps in virtualized renderers. Goal: Deliver a cohesive interaction that allows users to (1) collapse low-priority columns into an elastic overflow, (2) resize columns with proportional heuristics that are stable for virtualized lists, and (3) surface a lightweight density tuner with immediate visual feedback and persisted preferences.
design_decisions: Introduce an 'elastic collapse' affordance in the column header menu: toggling moves a column into a collapsed pill group to the right of headers instead of hiding permanently.

Proportional-resize uses a hybrid heuristic: initial drag respects explicit pixel delta for the active column, then redistributes remaining delta across visible flexible columns using weighted priorities to avoid reflow spikes in virtualization windows.
Density tuner is a compact popover with 'Compact / Comfortable / Spacious' presets plus a slider for fine-grained row height; slider updates are debounced for rendering performance.
Default persistence: workspace-level setting; allow per-user override stored in profile preferences. No automatic user migration — explicit opt-in on first open after release.
Telemetry: emit resize and collapse events (anonymized) to measure default weights effectiveness and identify high-friction paths.
alternatives_considered: Full column hiding: simpler but causes discoverability loss and breaks column reorder mental model for some power users.
Autoshrink text-with-ellipsis-only: low implementation cost but poor UX when numeric columns need legibility.
Server-side snapshotting of column widths: robust but requires API changes and increases coupling with Dedicated/Private deployments.
Density-only approach (no column collapse): reduces scope but fails to address horizontal space constraints on very wide tables.
accessibility_notes: Elastic collapse must be keyboard operable: toggle via header menu (Enter) and focus moves to the collapsed pill group; pills are reachable via Tab and announce their original header via aria-label.
Proportional-resize supports keyboard resize (+/-) on focused header; aria-live region will announce new width in characters and whether neighboring columns were adjusted.
Density tuner uses role=dialog with focus trap; changes announced as previews using polite aria-live to avoid overwriting screen reader navigation context.

For virtualized lists, ensure screen reader focus does not jump when virtualization window changes; when collapse triggers reflow, defer live announcements until after stabilizing render (200ms debounce).
engineering_notes: ENG must expose column priority weight on the column model; design will supply default weight mapping and a JSON schema for persisted preferences.
Virtualization window needs stable column widths between renders — debounce layout updates from resize handler and apply batched updates in runtime-1.19+ kernel path.
Backend: no schema changes expected; all preferences persisted client-side to start, with optional server sync in next iteration (ENG-20345).
Provide a feature flag (tables.elasticColumnCollapse) for canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle elastic-collapse on any column and collapsed columns appear as pills with original header name and tooltip.
Resizing a column updates widths using proportional heuristic and does not cause visible jitter in a 10k row virtualized table test harness.
Density tuner updates row height live in demo data and persists across reload for the user.
Keyboard-only flows (open header menu, toggle collapse, focus pills, resize via keyboard) pass manual a11y checklist.
No accessibility regressions introduced in existing table stories (automated a11y run must remain green).
Telemetry events for resize and collapse are emitted and documented.
Design review sign-off (PM + Eng + Accessibility) recorded in comments before merge.
